projectBackground.name: Industrial Microgrid — Packing Hall Feed
projectBackground.context: A new packing hall needs a 400 V feeder. The design must keep voltage drop low and protection coordinated.

manager.name: Lucía Fernández
manager.note: Every number needs a source and a margin. And nobody touches a conductor until it's proven dead.

assignment.title: Design the packing hall feeder
assignment.brief: Calculate load and drop, size protection, complete the load schedule in Excel and describe safe isolation.

documents.name: Cable Data
documents.note: Resistance 0.05 ohm per phase; cable rating 125 A.

tasks.title: Three-Phase Power
tasks.prompt: V = 400 V, I = 100 A, power factor 0.9. What is the real power P = sqrt(3) x V x I x pf in kW?
tasks.reasoning: Three-phase real power includes the sqrt(3) factor and pf.
tasks.mistake: Using single-phase formulas gives the wrong load.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Voltage Drop
tasks.prompt: A 100 A load on a cable of 0.05 ohm per phase. What is the voltage drop (V) using V = I x R?
tasks.reasoning: Drop must stay within the code limit.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring drop causes motor starting problems.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Breaker Selection
tasks.prompt: Design current Ib = 100 A and cable rating Iz = 125 A. Which breaker rating In is correct?
options: In between 100 A and 125 A so Ib <= In <= Iz
tasks.reasoning: The protective device must protect the cable and carry the load.
tasks.mistake: A breaker above Iz fails to protect the cable.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Safe Isolation
tasks.prompt: Before working on a circuit, what must you do?
options: Isolate, lock off, and prove dead with a tested voltage indicator
tasks.reasoning: Safe isolation is proven, not assumed.
tasks.mistake: Working on assumed-dead circuits causes fatalities.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Load Schedule (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Real power in kW (E = SQRT(3) x B x C x D / 1000) for each load. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: A load schedule underpins sizing of supply and protection.
tasks.mistake: Using apparent power as real power oversizes.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Method Statement
tasks.prompt: Write 3-5 sentences describing the safe isolation steps for the feeder.
tasks.modelAnswer: Identify the circuit from the drawing and notify operations, then open and lock off the supply with a personal lock and tag. Use an approved voltage indicator, proving it on a known live source, test the conductors dead and prove the indicator again. Apply earth where required and display warning notices. Only then start work, and keep the key with the person working.
tasks.reasoning: A good method follows a proven sequence with checks at each step.
tasks.mistake: Skipping the proving step defeats the process.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Dead That Wasn't
caseStudy.background: An electrician worked on a circuit that was off at the switch but fed from a second source. He received a severe shock and was off work for a year.
caseStudy.constraints: The drawing was out of date.
questions: What step would have caught it?
How do you keep drawings reliable?
caseStudy.solution: Voltara mandated lock, tag and prove-dead for every task and drawing updates after each change.
